Definition: from G5259 and G71; to lead (oneself) under, i.e. withdraw or retire (as if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively:--depart, get hence, go (a-)way.
BiblicalUsage: hypágō is the word for depart, get hence, go (a-)way. In Matthew 4:10, the text says "Get thee hence." In Mark 1:44, the text says "but go thy way."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading hypágō this way, I believe obedience is not drudgery; it is trusting that God's way is the good way. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Temptation in the Wilderness; Nicodemus Visits Jesus; Jesus Heals a Man with Leprosy
